summary:
Allwork.Space reports on a CBRE update showing Manhattan office leasing accelerated in July, with demand running ahead of historical averages and available space shrinking.

Key data points: July leasing hit 2.98 million square feet, 39% above the five-year monthly average. Year-to-date leasing reached 17.87 million square feet, a 2% increase over the same period the prior year. Office availability fell to 14.0%, down 40 basis points from June and 320 basis points year over year.

Net absorption was positive at 1.5 million square feet for the month and 6.58 million square feet year to date, meaning more space is being occupied than vacated.

On pricing, average asking rents held steady at $80.20 per square foot, flat versus June but up 4% year over year. The sublease market tightened, with sublease availability falling to 2.4% and average sublease asking rents flat year over year at $58.74 per square foot.

Renewals stayed active: 427,000 square feet in July and 6.36 million square feet year to date, which the piece reads as a sign that many companies are renewing existing space rather than relocating.

The item is a short market-statistics brief. It does not discuss workplace operations topics such as desk booking, hot desking, visitor management, RTO mandates or policy reaction, admin workload, or vendor procurement. Its relevance is limited to macro context on office demand recovery in a major US market.
